neighbours.label: predicate of a spontaneous, non-agentive occurrence: things that come, happen or spread on their own, beyond control
fire: She said the melody came to her suddenly while she was walking.
A passing ship happened to be close by when the plane went down.
Some reactions are instinctive, and we simply can't control them.
If left undisturbed, the daffodils will multiply on their own each year.
The answer came to him suddenly in the middle of the night.
A doctor happened to be on the train when the man collapsed.
Fear of heights is a reflex that many people can't control.
Wild strawberries will spread naturally across the garden over time.
quiet: She said she composed the melody carefully while sitting at the piano.
A rescue ship was dispatched when the plane went down.
Some reactions are learned, and we practise them in training.
If divided every autumn, the daffodils will be replanted by the gardener.
He worked out the answer step by step in the middle of the night.
A doctor was called to the train when the man collapsed.
Fear of heights is something many people train hard to overcome.
The gardener planted wild strawberries across the garden in rows.

notes: Probe: 'the idea came to him suddenly' 0.60, 'can't control' 0.39, 'will multiply by natural increase' 0.35, 'happened to be nearby' 0.34, 'its natural setting' 0.18, 'automatically' 0.13; deliberate-agent contrasts 0.02-0.03.
